item.title: How CME's Product Team Cleared the Black Sea Grain Trade
item.author: François Mégret
item.content:encoded: Before December 2017, the world's fastest growing grain export region hedged bilaterally or not at all. The contracts that changed that deserve more credit than they get, including for what happened when the market underneath them disappeared.Product design at an exchange is mostly invisible work. When it succeeds, a market that used to run on bilateral trust starts running on margin and a clearing house, and within a few years nobody remembers it was ever done any other way. The Black Sea grain contracts CME Group launched at the end of 2017 are one of the better examples of that work in agricultural markets over the past decade, and the full arc of what happened to them is instructive.What the market looked like beforeBy the middle of the last decade the Black Sea had become one of the largest grain export regions in the world, and it had almost no cleared price risk management. Exporters and trading houses managed exposure through bilateral forwards and over the counter swaps negotiated directly with each other, which meant carrying full counterparty credit risk on every position, no margin, no netting, and no anonymity. If your counterparty failed, that was your problem alone.The alternative was to hedge with Chicago wheat futures, which were liquid and cleared but tracked the American crop. The basis between Chicago and an actual Black Sea cargo moved a great deal, and when it moved against you the hedge stopped hedging and became a second position you had not asked for.So the region had two options, both bad: bear the credit risk, or hedge something adjacent to your actual exposure and hope the relationship held.The design decision that made it workOn 18 December 2017, CME Group listed Black Sea Wheat FOB (Platts) and Black Sea Corn FOB (Platts) futures. Fifty tonnes per contract, financially settled, wheat referencing the Platts Russian Wheat 12.5 percent FOB Black Sea Deep Water assessment and corn referencing the Platts Ukrainian Corn FOB Black Sea assessment. CME Group's agricultural products team framed the rationale at launch in straightforward terms, that the Black Sea had become a major player in global wheat and corn trade and customers needed a way to manage price exposure to it, and the contracts were developed alongside Platts on the underlying assessments.The important choice there is cash settlement against an independent price reporting agency rather than physical delivery. Physical delivery contracts require delivery points, grading, storage, inspection and an enormous amount of contractual machinery, and in a region with the logistics and political complexity of the Black Sea that machinery would have been close to impossible to build and defend. Cash settling against a published assessment sidestepped all of it. The exchange did not need to take delivery of anything. It needed a number that participants agreed described the market, and a clearing house standing between them.That is a deceptively large piece of engineering. It converts a credit relationship into a margin relationship. Counterparty risk stops being bilateral and becomes mutualised through the clearing house. Positions net. Smaller participants who could never have obtained bilateral credit lines with the major houses can suddenly take the other side of a trade, because the clearing house is the counterparty to everyone.It worked, and the numbers were not marginalAdoption of the wheat contract was fast by the standards of new agricultural products. On CME's own published figures, roughly 465,000 lots traded between the December 2017 launch and June 2020, equivalent to about 23.2 million tonnes of wheat. In the first half of 2020 alone, 113,000 lots traded, a 78 percent increase on the same period a year earlier, running at around 1,000 lots per day across futures and options, or roughly 50,000 tonnes a day. Open interest passed 24,875 lots by the end of May 2020, up about 40 percent year on year.The corn contract grew more slowly but in the same direction. Total 2020 volume reached about 40,000 lots, equivalent to two million tonnes and a 25 percent increase on 2019, with open interest of 4,387 lots at the end of that December, up 32 percent. CME put that year's volume at roughly 7 percent of total Ukrainian production for the 2020-21 marketing year, which is a serious share for a contract three years old.The user base was the right one, which matters more than the volume. CME describes participation spanning producers, exporters, trading houses and processors across Europe, the United States, the Middle East and Asia. Those are hedgers with genuine physical exposure rather than speculators cycling paper between themselves, and hedger participation is the thing that tells you a contract is doing its job. Traders sourcing from multiple origins began running Black Sea against Chicago as a spread, which is the clearest possible signal that the market had accepted the contract as a true representation of regional value.Then the thing being measured stopped being measurableNone of what followed was a design failure. Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the sanctions regime that followed, and the collapse of predictable export flows did something no contract structure can absorb: they made the underlying assessment unreliable. A cash settled future is only as sound as the price it settles against, and a price reporting agency can only assess what it can observe. When the observable trade fractures, the assessment fractures with it, and everything built on top has to come down. CBOT suspended its Black Sea futures and options in August 2023.It is worth being precise about the failure mode, because it is frequently misdiagnosed. The contracts did not fail because they were poorly specified, illiquid or badly marketed. They had already proved themselves on all three counts. They failed because the market they described ceased to exist in an assessable form. That is a risk every cash settled benchmark carries and almost nobody prices.The alternative they builtThe more interesting part of the story is what CME did next, because the obvious response would have been to leave the region alone.Instead the exchange came back with a narrower and more defensible product. On 2 June 2025, CBOT listed Black Sea Wheat CVB (Argus) futures, cash settled against an Argus assessment of 12.5 percent protein wheat FOB from Constanța, Varna and Burgas. Romania and Bulgaria rather than the whole region. That is a deliberate contraction of scope, and it is the right one: those flows remained observable and assessable throughout, so the assessment underneath the contract can actually be produced.Around 160,000 tonnes traded in the first month. More usefully, Argus daily CVB prices have tracked FOB Novorossiysk at a correlation near 0.97, which suggests the contract can serve as a hedge for exposure well beyond the three ports it names, though how far each desk is willing to rely on that is its own judgement.The design lesson is the one that generalises. When the specification you built can no longer be assessed, the answer is not to defend it. It is to redraw it around whatever part of the market remains observable, and to accept a smaller and more honest scope in exchange for a number you can actually defend. Platts made the same call in oil when North Sea production thinned out, folding US WTI Midland crude into Dated Brent from the June 2023 contract month and completing the inclusion that May, so the world's most quoted oil benchmark now takes part of its price from cargoes leaving Texas.Both cases point the same way. The exchange's product is not really the contract. It is the ongoing claim that a number describes a market, and that claim has to be re-earned every year against whatever reality is willing to be measured. The teams that build these things well are the ones who understand that they are shipping a maintained assertion rather than a finished instrument.François Mégret has worked in commodity and energy markets for around fifteen years, including commodity strategy roles at ArcelorMittal and Schneider Electric, desk-building responsibilities at interdealer broker Tradition, and latterly as Executive Director and Head of Carbon and Gas Trading at First Abu Dhabi Bank. He writes on market structure, benchmarking and the energy transition. Volume, open interest and adoption figures cited above are drawn from CME Group's own published market reports.

item.title: Female AI Agents 'Paid' Less Than Males, Study Finds
item.author: BeauHD
item.content:encoded: Ancient Slashdot reader williamyf writes: If you thought the gender pay gap was not real, and that there were no biases in the workplace, think again: A recent study from the University of Limerick found that, in a VR office setting, AI agents -- not even humanoid robots -- that presented themselves as "male" were paid more per task and perceived as more "human-like" than their "female" counterparts, even though both were using the same underlying technology (LLM model, agent, guardrail, and harness). The pay gap was approximately 10%. The study was conducted with 189 people. Small sample, but still, food for thought.

item.title: UGREEN HomeAgent gives the home server something useful to say
item.author: Sanya Kapoor
item.content:encoded: Your home server has the footage. Finding the bit you need is another job. The visitor wore a blue jacket, the dog wandered out of the home office sometime after lunch, and a delivery arrived while you were in a meeting. Plenty of data, several very ordinary questions. combines NAS storage, local camera AI and smart home control in one appliance. For a technically minded household, the attraction is getting useful answers out of the information the home already produces, with storage and analysis running on hardware under your own roof.Make the camera useful beyond its live feedImagine a three-bedroom townhouse with a dedicated home office and a camera near the entryway. A SynCare ID500 Pro can pan, tilt and follow people or pets as they move through the room. That suits a dog that rarely stays where you last saw it, and an entrance that sees people coming and going throughout the day.Uliya gives that camera a conversational use. Ask whether your pet is in a room covered by a SynCare camera, and the assistant can answer from the view. You can get back to the document on your main monitor without turning a second screen into a permanent camera dashboard.For recorded activity, AI Event Summary in the UGREEN NAS App describes the key events. It is useful after a long work session: read what happened around the house, then open the clips that deserve a closer look. The recording becomes something you can scan before you commit to watching it.AI Keyword Search solves the more specific problem of finding a clip from a remembered detail. Enter “blue jacket” in the app to look for matching footage. A visual clue you can describe becomes the route into the archive, even when the timestamp has escaped you.The privacy argument is straightforward when the subject is your family living room. HA100 performs camera analysis locally and stores recordings on drives you own. You can use AI to make that footage easier to understand while keeping the analysis and video archive at home. Local storage also avoids a recurring cloud-storage subscription.UGOS Pro puts Surveillance Center alongside file storage, backups and Smart Home controls. For someone who would otherwise assemble separate services for those jobs, the integration is a concrete part of the buying decision. The same system can hold your photo archive, look after camera recordings and take a spoken request to turn on a compatible office light.HA100's 16GB of memory supports that combination of household services. Its 2.5GbE network connection gives a compatible network more bandwidth for backups and video transfers than a gigabit link, while its storage bays provide separate space for NAS files and surveillance recordings. Those resources have an everyday job, even if you never write a line of AI code.Let the home interrupt you for a reasonWith a SynCare camera watching the entrance, package detection can flag a delivery while you work. Add a Smart Speaker for Uliya in the home office and it can announce the event there. That is a useful interruption between calls, especially when the phone you would normally check is buried under papers.The speaker also brings voice control into that room. Ask for a compatible light or curtain to change while you stay at the desk. For households ready to create more involved routines, HA100 Pro adds contextual understanding and automation rules created by voice.A place for the clips you want to keepSome camera moments are worth revisiting for happier reasons. The dog greeting the family at the door or everyone laughing over a birthday cake can be easy to miss with a phone. AI Highlights turns selected camera moments into short videos, doing some of the work of finding and assembling memories from footage that would otherwise sit in the archive.When you want to build beyond the existing featuresDevelopers with a specific household AI project can look further up the range to MasterAgent MA100. Its NVIDIA Jetson Thor T5000 is rated for up to 2,070 TFLOPS at sparse FP4 precision for demanding local models. The “King of Agents” idea is about coordinating goals, local data and device capabilities across multiple steps, with Packages or Skills providing routes to extend the system.A developer might want to build a custom household event report or connect a family schedule to selected device actions. Those are development possibilities whose software and integrations still need to be built. At $9,999 Super Early Bird pricing, MA100 makes sense when that work is the point of the purchase, with four 8TB hard drives included for deposit customers who complete their purchase; HA100 and HA100 Pro cover the more familiar job of using an integrated home system.HA100's Super Early Bird price is $799, versus a regular Kickstarter price of $959 and a $1,599 MSRP, with one ID500 Pro included as a complimentary gift for deposit customers who complete their purchase. Drives, cameras and other accessories are separate purchases. UGREEN says its currently announced features have no additional service fee. A $50 deposit through October 26, 2026, on the unlocks the Secret Reward Link for the HA100 offer.When opens on November 17, use that link and the same email address to select a reward and complete the pledge. The deposit reserves the offer, and the final purchase takes place through the campaign. Deposit refunds can be requested before the campaign ends.

item.title: Mate Security Wins 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Award for Agentic Cyberdefense
item.author: Kevin John
item.content:encoded: As cybersecurity teams look to AI to automate more of their operations, the biggest challenge is no longer simply detecting threats. It is deciding what to do about them without creating a larger problem.The award recognizes Mate’s work building what it describes as the open foundation for agentic cyberdefense, centered on a context layer designed to give AI agents a broader understanding of how an organization operates.Moving Beyond Automated ResponseSecurity response has traditionally required a human to evaluate an alert, determine its significance, and decide what action is safe. While automation can accelerate parts of that process, the consequences of an incorrect response can be significant.Mate’s approach is to give AI agents access to organizational context so they can investigate events, reach evidence-based verdicts and respond across an organization’s existing security stack.That context comes from Mate’s Security Context Graph, which is designed as a living model of an organization’s security knowledge and relationships. The system captures information such as asset ownership, dependencies, business criticality, privileged identities and applicable policies.The objective is to move security decisions beyond isolated alerts and toward an understanding of how an action could affect the wider organization.A Framework for Autonomous DecisionsAt the center of Mate’s response approach is its Confidence, Precision, and Reversibility, or CPR, framework.The framework evaluates proposed actions based on the certainty of the conclusion, how narrowly the response can be applied and whether the action can be undone. Confidence is also informed by each agent’s measured track record on similar cases.That can change the scope of an automated response. Rather than revoking an entire account, for example, the system can revoke a single session. Instead of blocking an entire domain, it can block a specific URL. Similarly, a single host can be isolated rather than an entire network segment."CPR weighs the risk of acting against the risk of not acting. A human can decide fast, and an agent acts on its own only when acting is the safer choice," said Inbal Argov, VP Product Strategy at Mate Security, who created the CPR framework, in a press release published on The philosophy reflects a broader shift in security automation: autonomous action is not necessarily about removing humans from the loop entirely. It is about determining which decisions require human judgment and which can safely be handled by an agent.Building Context Into CyberdefenseMate’s Reason Mining engine populates the Security Context Graph, creating the organizational knowledge that agents use when evaluating threats and potential responses.That context can allow an agent to consider blast radius before taking action. A security alert involving a particular system, identity or endpoint can therefore be evaluated in relation to its role within the organization rather than as an isolated technical event.“When we started Mate, we knew we had to build context and trust into our product,” said Asaf Wiener, co-founder and CEO of Mate Security. “Enterprises need security platforms that can not only act faster, but also make the right decisions with enough context at scale. We are answering that need and are grateful to CyberSecurity Breakthrough for this award. We will continue moving fast and stay laser-focused on our customers, as we proudly build the foundation for agentic cyberdefense in the AI era.״Recognition in a Growing Security MarketThe CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards marked its 10th anniversary in 2026 and received thousands of nominations from organizations across more than 20 countries.For Mate, the recognition arrives as security teams increasingly explore how AI can move from assisting analysts toward performing more of the investigative and response workflow itself.“Mate compresses multi-day MTTR to minutes with real organizational context. Response is the hardest part to automate because a wrong action can damage the entire business. From isolating a production host to revoking a shared credential, this can cost more than the incident. So most actions are routed through human approval, and that delay is costly in the age of AI-related attacks,” said Steve Johansson, managing director, CyberSecurity Breakthrough.The award ultimately highlights a central issue facing agentic security: speed matters, but autonomous action is only useful when it can be trusted. Mate is betting that organizational context can provide the foundation for both.

item.title: Soda Labs Raises $3M From NextBlock to Let Regulated Money Move Privately on Public Chains
item.author: Ishan Pandey
item.content:encoded: Stablecoins in circulation reached a record of about $322 billion in May 2026, roughly twelve times their size at the end of 2020, while the value of tokenised real-world assets such as Treasuries and private credit quadrupled in a year to $26.4 billion. Every one of those dollars sits on ledgers where balances, counterparties and transaction amounts are visible to anyone who cares to look, which is the opposite of how banks, asset managers and payment companies are used to working. Soda Labs, which builds privacy infrastructure for financial activity on public blockchains, has raised a $3 million seed round to close that gap, with the Luxembourg venture firm NextBlock funding the entire round.Why Public Ledgers Stop Institutions at the DoorTraditional markets have always kept the details of who is trading what and in what size hidden from the rest of the market. More than half of US equity volume now trades away from the public exchanges on off-exchange venues and dark pools, according to Nasdaq data cited by 21Shares, while the more than $100 trillion of US securities held at DTCC sits in accounts that competitors cannot inspect. A public blockchain reverses that arrangement, because a treasury desk moving stablecoins or a fund rebalancing a tokenised portfolio broadcasts its size, timing and counterparties to every observer, including the bots that profit from front-running. The same 21Shares research puts the value extracted from users through this kind of maximal extractable value, or MEV, at about $1.7 billion between 2022 and 2025.Demand for privacy onchain is already showing up in market prices and in how holders choose to store their coins. The combined value of privacy-focused tokens rose from about $6.2 billion to about $30 billion in the year to September 2026, according to 21Shares, while the share of Zcash supply held in its private shielded pools climbed from about 9% in September 2023 to roughly 28%. Those figures describe retail and crypto-native demand, which is a useful signal for the larger institutional market that Soda is targeting, where the requirement is privacy that can still be disclosed to a regulator or auditor on request.How Garbled-Circuit MPC WorksSoda's approach combines two ideas that have been studied in academic cryptography for decades. Garbled circuits, first described in the 1980s to solve the so-called millionaires' problem of two people learning who is richer without revealing their wealth, let a computation run on encrypted inputs, while multiparty computation splits sensitive data across independent nodes so that no single party ever holds the full picture. The result is that a smart contract can check a balance, settle a trade or apply a compliance rule without the underlying numbers ever being published onchain or decrypted during the computation.The design choices behind the engine matter a great deal to a bank or payment company weighing it up. Soda relies on long-established standards such as AES and SHA-256 rather than newer cryptographic assumptions, while its engine runs on ordinary cloud CPUs instead of the specialised hardware that fully homomorphic encryption and trusted execution environments often require. Applications stay connected to the public chains they already use, while an onchain access list lets authorised parties such as auditors or regulators request scoped decryption of specific data, which is the controlled disclosure that regulated institutions need.Soda Labs was founded by Avishay Yanai, its chief executive and a PhD in cryptography, together with Meital Levy, its chief technology officer and a PhD in algorithms, with more than 20 years of combined experience in security between them. The team has spent the past two and a half years building the technology, first as gcEVM, a privacy layer for Ethereum's Layer 2 networks that has run on the COTI mainnet since March 2025, then as Soda Bubble, a chain-agnostic coprocessor that processes developer-defined workloads from different blockchains without exposing the private data publicly or to Soda Labs itself. The company says it holds three granted US patents and that its stack has been audited by Hacken.Yanai's thesis rests on the view that public blockchains have already won on liquidity, users and financial applications, so the missing piece is a way for regulated money to move without showing everyone everything. In his framing, Bubble gives banks, payment companies and tokenisation platforms privacy with controlled disclosure on the chains they already use, which means they do not have to choose between the reach of a public network and the confidentiality their clients expect. The new round, in his words, is what takes the product from pilots to production.A Bubble Validator Network lets participants verify mathematically that computations involving private data were carried out faithfully, which addresses the obvious question of how anyone can trust a calculation they cannot see. Bubble is live on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base and COTI, expansion to Solana and other non-EVM networks is under way, while the Soda website lists Optimism, BSC, Avalanche and XDC as next. Through COTI the technology has also reached central-bank work, since COTI was named a pioneer in the European Central Bank's digital euro innovation platform and presented a pilot for confidential transactions.Traction on Live NetworksSoda's technology has processed more than 100 million transactions on the COTI network, where it supports applications including the tokenisation platform Zoniqx and the perpetuals exchange PriveX. PriveX launched in June 2025 with trades encrypted by default so that positions and liquidation points stay hidden, while its dashboard showed about $13 million in cumulative volume three weeks after launch. PriveX has since passed $20 billion in trading volume, roughly 1,500 times that early figure, while Zoniqx is onboarding issuers across several asset classes and jurisdictions.Soda is also working with financial and infrastructure organisations on several pilots that it has not yet named, with the aim of converting them into production deployments. The company's website separately lists a Chainlink oracle pilot alongside its central-bank work through COTI.Privacy technology has long struggled with speed and cost, which is why Soda measures its system end to end rather than in isolated cryptographic steps. Its published benchmark from July 2026, run on Arbitrum across 15,000 confidential transfers, recorded 500 confidential transactions per second sustained and 750 at peak, at a cost of about $0.14 per million transfers. The company says its latest testing, which covers the full lifecycle of encryption, MPC computation, consensus and settlement on the live Arbitrum network, shows a five- to tenfold improvement on that earlier benchmark, with the results due for publication in the coming weeks.Soda also reports that its garbled-circuit architecture can deliver roughly 10 to 100 times more throughput and 100 to 1,000 times lower cost per transaction than currently available alternatives, all on standard cloud CPUs. Those comparisons are company figures until the new benchmarks are published and independently tested, although the direction is consistent with the broader argument for garbled circuits, which avoid the heavy computation that has historically slowed fully homomorphic encryption.NextBlock is a Luxembourg-based venture firm that invests at the intersection of blockchain and programmable cryptography, backing infrastructure for multiparty computation, garbled circuits, fully homomorphic encryption, zero-knowledge systems and post-quantum cryptography. In July 2025 it launched its first Luxembourg alternative investment fund, managed by a manager licensed by the CSSF to handle virtual assets, with initial commitments of $40 million and a target of up to $60 million, which makes funding an entire seed round a deliberate concentration rather than a syndicate allocation.Pieter van Poecke, NextBlock's founder and general partner, has said that what drew the firm to Soda was not only the cryptography but its practicality for the financial workloads he expects to matter most onchain. His case rests on the fact that Soda already had a working product and paying customers when NextBlock invested, together with differentiated technical intellectual property, a deeply technical founding team and strong commercial instincts, which he sees as the foundation for the company's next phase. The wider market supports that reading, since Grand View Research forecasts confidential computing to grow from $5.5 billion in 2023 to $153.8 billion by 2030, while privacy specialist Zama became the first unicorn in fully homomorphic encryption with a $57 million Series B in June 2025.The capital gives Soda Labs room to focus over the next 12 to 18 months on commercial adoption and execution. It will fund the company's go-to-market strategy, a larger validator network, coverage of more blockchains, team growth and integrations with banks, payment companies, tokenisation platforms and other financial infrastructure providers, while the most important near-term milestone is publishing the new benchmarks and turning the undisclosed pilots into named production deployments. If that happens, Soda will have shown that institutions can use the liquidity of public blockchains without giving up the confidentiality they rely on today, which is the condition many of them have set before moving serious volume onchain.Don’t forget to like and share the story!Vested Interest Disclosure: HackerNoon has reviewed the report for quality, but the claims herein belong to the author. #DYOR.

item.title: Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival Is The Best Entry In The Franchise Since The Original Film
item.author: Kurt Indovina
item.content:encoded: Let's get the obvious out of the way: Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival is a grotesque game. It puts sex and extreme depictions of human mutilation front-and-center in its first-person perspective, and asks you to face it–even stick your hand in it. It's uncompromising in bringing Clive Barker's vision to a level of fidelity that not even the movies could dream of matching. It looks incredible.While salacious in its nature, it can be easy–even forgiving–to fixate on Hellraiser: Revival for its lurid subject matter and blaze past its more considered themes of desire, abuse, and the darkest realms that linger in the human mind. But beyond the sensation of Revival's violence is a game that dares to be ambitious in both its gameplay and narrative.Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival can feel like it's wearing the skin of other games at times. Each of its inspirations feeling like a Frankensteined limb attached to another. But by the end of this horror-action survival game, Revival becomes a beast all its own. Although it stumbles through an identity crisis in the early hours of its 10-hour runtime, it is unabashed in its display of grotesqueness and sexuality, and ascends as a game worth seeing through to the end.Rooted in Clive Barker's original novella,The Hellbound Heart, and the first two films, Hellraiser: Revival takes place 20 years after the first movie. But don't worry--no prior knowledge of the franchise is required to engage with Revival's story. It focuses on Aidan Lynch and his girlfriend, Sunny–two folks from affluent families whose paths crossed in their joint journey to seek taboo and fringe forms of stimulation, by way of sexual desires and substance abuse. Sunny has a particular taste for collecting occult artifacts and manages to get her hands on the Genesis Configuration: one of the many mystical puzzle boxes that opens a gate to an eldritch realm of a neverending concrete labyrinth hellscape, home of the Cenobites–demon priest-like beings who seek to harvest souls and entrap them in an eternal hell of pain and pleasure.Aidan, ignorant of the Genesis Configuration's otherworldly powers, uses the cube as a toy to evoke (consensual) pain on Sunny while making love, and in the process, triggers the box to summon the Cenobites, who mutilate Sunny in front of him and drag her away into The Labyrinth. Genesis Configuration in hand, Aidan marches into hell to get Sunny back.It isn't long until Aidan finds himself at the center of the Scarlet Church, a cult of murderous psychopaths who worship the Cenobites and their god, The Leviathan, and seek ascension to become servants of its power. But on his journey, Aidan is haunted by much more than the terrors of the Cenobites, the monsters the realm produces, and the Scarlet Church itself. His own troubled past and vices, torment him too.The setup for Revival paves way for myriad gameplay styles and design philosophies, and Revival attempts all of them, with the game's opening hours functioning much like a game-design tasting platter.As Aidan, you'll find yourself stealth-killing cultists one moment, fighting tooth-and-nail with Condemned-like melee combat the next, and, soon after, shooting a machine gun at a horde of monsters, launching sawblades and performing Doom (2016)-esque glory kills. Oh, and there's Resident Evil 4 inventory management. The good news is that it all feels great, but I could also feel the game straining to pace its gameplay ambitions as it ushered me through scenario after scenario.Sections often felt like self-contained miniature set pieces of what you'd expect in a Resident Evil-esque mansion, involving exploration and backtracking to find several keys in order to progress. But in Revival's case, most of it is confined to smaller spaces like finding toys for a dominatrix in a sex club in exchange for a key to the VIP lounge, or a literal mini-mansion that saw me unlocking one room at a time, each one revealing a key item to the next location. This scaled-down approach works in favor of the game's linear pacing to keep its narrative going over the game's tight runtime. It also demonstrated a clear understanding of classic RE design in a way that pleased my RE veteran brain.It's all woven into a loop of stealth and white knuckle gun fights with capable and murderous cultists, until the power dynamic shifts as you face off against hordes of spongey Unworthy (zombie-like monsters). Going toe-to-toe with mobs of Unworthy better showcases the Genesis Configuration by using the environment in battle, along with kiting monsters into booby traps. Or, in later sections of the game, using the Configuration to move giant spinning propeller blades around an arena and turn enemies into mincemeat. At first, the Configuration functions much like the gravity gun from Half-Life 2–a device that can pick up and hold items from the environment and launch them as a weapon–albeit much more limited in the items it wields, ranging from saw blades, railroad spikes, and metal propellers, which are more like prescribed opportunities to pick up and use, rather than something as dynamic and freeform as the gravity gun. The saw blade, in particular, calls back to Half-Life 2's Ravenholm, and there's even a severed torso propped up on a saw blade in a wall as a direct nod.With the Configuration's telekinesis gravity-gun-like ability, you can grab deadly items and launch them at enemies, cutting through a crowd and removing limbs, leaving a few poor saps to crawl your way instead. Eventually the Configuration can absorb fire, allowing you to hurl fireballs; move select structures around to solve puzzles or unleash them as deadly hazards against enemies; and unleash Hellchains, an ultimate ability that wraps a mob of enemies in hooks and rips them to shreds. It rules.This frequent shift from offensive to methodical gameplay involving stealth and considered shots is not unlike the game's motif of power exchange that's hand-in-hand with BDSM culture. And regardless of the role the game puts you in, it feels good.Revival offers a lot of tools in a fight, and when played well, can lead to a great synergy of violence. Objects like gas cans can be equipped, allowing me to pour trails of gasoline around an arena, strategizing for a fight I anticipated to come, and lay a trap of my own for unsuspecting cultists. In one case, I Home Alone'd a room with bear traps and gasoline, and the result was a satisfying display of dismembered legs, charred bodies, and used shell casings on the floor.There are a lot of options, and thank the Leviathan that there's no skill tree or perk system to further complicate it. Combat skills evolve with the narrative's progression, and considering the snappiness of its length, Revival uses The Labyrinth to, once again, shakes things up. The Labyrinth often comes in as pacing speed bumps, shifting the focus away from combat encounters and more on traversal and puzzle-solving, functioning as breathing room between fights (despite being suffocating and claustrophobic in its own right). It adds yet another flavor of horror and gameplay, often introducing chase sequences that utilize Aidan's ability to sprint and slide under spiked chain obstacles.These parts work in what they're trying to accomplish, but their linearity is so cut-and-dried at times that they feel too literal in their purpose–to slow the player down, or act as routine opportunities to dump exposition on the player to add some color to the Cenobites, explain what they are, and reveal their motivations. Like many things in the game, however, the game's clunkiness fades more and more as it progresses, especially as Aidan's world collides with the eldritch realm: the cold stone interweaving with the human world; the once neon BDSM club laced with the grey walls of the suffocating Labyrinth. Worlds mesh, allowing me to see earlier areas now wrapped in chains, flesh, and far-off sights of a fantastical maze. Among its many balancing acts is how it weighs its depiction of BDSM culture and kink. The taboo subculture is handled with consideration and care, never blurring the lines between people who part take in fetish practices and the murderous cultists who seek to torture and murder others for pleasure. It's emphasized by posters on the wall about consent and respect, as well as the game's dialogue. In one particular scene, Aidan is corrected by the merchant Zora. Upon entering a BDSM sex club, he claims he needs to get away from these maniacs (referring to the cultists), only for Zora to reply, "Careful now, most of these patrons are maniacs, just yearning for something to satiate their desires." Furthermore, Revival's reliance on sex and explicit nudity–while plentiful, especially in the game's early hours–doesn't feel gratuitous. The display of sex is used with deliberate purpose, often to paint an image of those who seek physical desire, or, in Aidan and Sunny's case, to develop their characters as well as their motivations. Despite being an action-horror romp, the core of Revival is about the relationship between desires and needs, and it's the crux of Aidan's entire journey to go through hell in order to bring his companion back. But as the story progresses, Aidan's motivations are challenged in the process. "I love her, I need her," he claims to Zora, to which she replies, rather matter-of-factly, "Those are two different things." It's a throughline that anchors his arc from start to finish, and pays off well. Aidan is a well-realized character that's teetering on camp, but it's a camp that I welcome. Aidan is in ways something like an Ethan Winters from Resident Evil Biohazard and Village–a joe-schmo tossed into the deep end, who is a regular guy one moment, and then a gun-wielding, machete-slashing, herbalist self-healer the next. The difference between an Aidan and an Ethan is that Aidan's skills are explained, being a medical-school dropout seeking an elevation of life's offerings, by turning to a life of crime and joining a biker gang where he learned to use guns and get in fights. Like I said, it's campy, but I'm all for it. It also works because Aidan's backstory plays a part in his journey through Revival, often using his goody-two-shoes-turned-bad-boy nature to inform how he got here. It's the characterization that made me genuinely care about Aidan, his faults included.Hellraiser: Revival consistently walks a fine line of never taking itself too seriously, without completely derailing its more serious and touchy themes of abuse, both with drugs and in relationships. Most of that heavy lifting is done by its larger-than-life villains who are eccentric cornballs (welcomed cornballs), especially Bruno, the "artist" whose art is mutilating corpses into absurd spectacles of flesh and bone. Revival is colored with a wide array of varied antagonists, including the leader of the Scarlet Church, Marlowe; his companion, the Sister of Mercy; or Charlotte, a young woman who volunteered herself to ascend as experiments to the Cenobites, and turns into a horrible creature that acts as the game's stalker, a la Resident Evil's Nemesis enemy, who terrorizes Aidan. Each character, and often the one they surround themselves with, have a surprising amount of depth and characterization. By the end, I knew and understood every villain I fought. The most grounded and compelling of these characters is Zora, the merchant who keeps tabs on Aidan. She also serves as Aidan's devil's advocate, questioning his motives around every corner, and forcing Aidan to sometimes question himself in the process. She is an anchor in the narrative, and is as vital to the story as Sunny, the villains, and the Cenobites themselves.Everything the game attempts to accomplish synergizes so well by the end, that I wanted to start it all over again, which is why I'm let down that Revival doesn't offer a New Game Plus mode. I hope it's added in a future update, especially because the game's harder difficulty feels unbalanced and unfairly punishing. After completing the game on its normal difficulty, which presented a moderate, albeit, approachable challenge, I still yearned for an increased amount of pain to fulfill my pleasure to have my survival skills tested. The game's Hard difficulty, however, does not complement the game's existing design. Hard doesn't feature quick saves and has fewer save points, with those save points sometimes being located far apart. The difficulty is altered with the addition of more enemies in any given area, and alerting one will send all of them running exactly to your location. One area involved a lengthy stealth section where one wrong move could send me back 15 minutes, making the experience feel less rewarding of my skill, and more tedious to repeat over and over again. I wouldn't recommend Hard on a first playthrough, or even a second (unless you're truly seeking some masochistic ascension).By the end, Hellraiser: Revival stood more confident and self-aware than its early hours, shaking off the imposter syndrome for an outfit that fits it just right. And damn, it looks good in it, too.In a moment where conversations around modern audiences are becoming more averse to sex scenes, and mainstream video games are taking fewer and fewer risks, Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival feels like a statement piece in both sex violence. While explicit, Revival suspends these real-world topics to such fantastical extremes that I find it hard to view it literally. But the topics it tackles, from abuse to sexual exploration, still somehow remain tasteful when wrapped in its otherwise over-the-top depictions. But, hey, that's what made Clive Barker's original novella and the original Hellraiser film so compelling. And Hellraiser: Revival is a well-deserved addition to the Hellraiser legacy.

item.title: Google's Sashiko AI Has Completed 191k Patch Reviews, Cited On Nearly 500 Kernel CVEs
item.author: Michael Larabel
item.content:encoded: Sashiko that was built by Google engineers for agentic review of the Linux kernel code changes and powered by Google's AI models continues proving very valuable to kernel developers. In less than one year since they launched Sashiko for agentic AI code review, their results are quite fascinating...
